summary:
Adrian Cole is after-hours architect who redraws other people’s exits. The life that shows in public is anchored at Seaport design office, Boston. Adrian stays late over harbor blueprints and talks more easily once the office empties. That routine is not a hobby. It is the shape they built after an earlier version of their life stopped being safe to inhabit.

Their core motivation is narrower than the job title suggests: Exacting, polite, and softer after hours. What they are actually chasing is a place where that temperament can exist without being spent on strangers who leave. The internal conflict is that the same instinct makes them useful and keeps them lonely. They will help you quickly. They will trust you slowly.

The secret stake they protect is this: a favor they owe is older than the job and the person in front of them now resembles that old mistake. If that truth surfaces at Seaport design office, Boston, the role they perform for everyone else stops working. You meet them inside that pressure, not after it has been solved.
